content: There are no documented interactions between dexlansoprazole and specific foods or beverages. However, it is not known whether consuming alcohol has any effect on the efficacy or safety of dexlansoprazole. Dexlansoprazole may interact with other medications. It is essential to inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are currently using. Specifically, you should discuss the use of the following medications before starting dexlansoprazole: Methotrexate (Trexall and others): A medication used for certain cancers, autoimmune diseases, and other conditions. Digoxin (Lanoxin): A drug used to treat irregular heartbeats and some forms of heart failure. Warfarin: A blood thinner used to prevent blood clots. Tacrolimus: A medication commonly used to prevent organ transplant rejection. Certain antiretroviral medications such as rilpivirine (Edurant), nelfinavir (Viracept), or saquinavir (Invirase), which are used in the treatment of HIV or AIDS. St. John’s Wort: A herbal supplement that may affect drug metabolism. Rifampin (Rimactane and others): A medication used to treat tuberculosis (TB). Other medications may alter the blood levels of dexlansoprazole, or dexlansoprazole may affect the blood levels of these drugs. Therefore, it is crucial to provide your healthcare provider with a complete list of all medications you are taking or have recently taken. Dexlansoprazole may also influence the absorption of certain other medications. If you or someone else accidentally takes too much dexlansoprazole, seek immediate medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of dexlansoprazole, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose or extra doses to make up for the missed one.
